The *Kesakārīvimānavatthu* ("Kesakārī’s Mansion", Vv 17) is a verse text in the *Vimānavatthu* section of the Pali canon [SuttaCentral]. The text centers on an exchange in which the deity Sakka asks what meritorious deeds allowed a particular *deva* to achieve a radiant splendor comparable to that of a Brahmā [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral records six modern translations of the text across six languages [SuttaCentral].

Textual reuse is primarily documented within the traditional exegesis: the DharmaNexus database records 12 matching passages (comprising 2,234 shared characters) between the canonical verses and the *Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā*, with the most extensive match spanning segments 1.1–4.4 of the text and sections 723–733 of the commentary [DharmaNexus].
